subject: Outbound binding validation and allowlist acceptance for EdgeProxy-managed private endpoints
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Martin <security@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health SRE <sre@acmehealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Outbound binding validation and allowlist acceptance for EdgeProxy-managed private endpoints

Hi Lydia / Acme SRE team,

Following our onboarding call, sharing the concrete ask and proposed acceptance criteria so we can move to a short test window. This thread covers the IP allowlist / firewall and egress controls for the Redwood Private endpoint you are hosting in your VPC.

High-level requirements from Acme (recap):
- Per-tenant outbound mapping (we will present tenant-specific NAT IPs or identifiable header)
- Proof of possession for static/ephemeral egress IPs
- Port/FQDN allowlist (minimal ports; 443 preferred)
- Audit logs and 90-day retention for outbound connections tied to tenant identifier

What Redwood will provide for the acceptance run:
1) Egress IP manifest: CSV with candidate IPs, ASN and expected allocation windows (attached: egress-ip-map.csv).
2) Evidence bundle: signed certificate of ownership + short PKI chain and sample tcpdump of connection to our control plane (we will upload a zip to the Drive link below).
3) TLS behavior: we support SNI-preserved TLS; optional mTLS for control-plane endpoints.
4) Port and FQDN guidance: we recommend 443 outbound to these FQDNs only; fallback to proxy pattern documented in runbook.

Acceptance criteria (proposed):
- Test window: 48 hours where Acme allows the candidate IPs; during that time we will run scripted checks to confirm connections originate from listed IPs or provide tenant-mapping header X-Redwood-Tenant.
- If you need per-tenant NATs we can allocate ephemeral / reserved mapping; otherwise we will assert tenant identity via signed header (we prefer minimal new NATs).
- Audit evidence: we will deliver tokenized logs containing timestamps, src egress IP, destination FQDN, tenant-id for the window.

Please confirm: (A) whether Acme requires NATed-per-tenant IPs (vs signed header), (B) minimum test window for ops to validate, and (C) any additional gating (legal, procurement).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 30-min run-through if useful.

Ben Carter
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: egress-ip-map.csv (CSV)
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lydia Martin <security@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health SRE <sre@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Outbound binding validation and allowlist acceptance for EdgeProxy-managed private endpoints

Ben — adding a few technical clarifications from the runtime/ops side that will affect what you ask the Acme firewall team to allow.

- NAT behavior: Redwood Private runtimes can be configured two ways: (1) shared egress IPs per-region (cheapest), (2) per-tenant NAT pools (one-to-one mapping) — option (2) requires reservation at provisioning and is subject to IP scarcity in the region.
- Proof-of-possession: we will produce a signed JSON manifest, timestamped, containing the IPs and the private runtime instance id. This manifest will be signed with our platform key and pushed to the Drive link (see related_links).
- If Acme prefers not to allow broad ranges, we can also support an intermediate proxy (we'll present a short-lived client cert to the proxy). In that pattern, the outbound source will still be a small set of IPs but we will supply a JWT or header for tenant correlation.
- Ports: by default we only need 443 outbound to these FQDNs: control.redwood.ai, metrics.redwood.ai, model-pull.redwood.ai. If your IDS requires explicit FQDNs we will provide the full list.
- Audit logs: logs will be tokenized (no model payloads) and include: time, src_eip, dst_fqdn, tenant_id, request_id. We can deliver these over SFTP or push to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) — please indicate preference.

I'll prepare the evidence bundle and a short runbook for the on-test steps (attachment: private-endpoint-runbook-v1.md).

— David
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: private-endpoint-runbook-v1.md (text)
From: Lydia Martin <security@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Outbound binding validation and allowlist acceptance for EdgeProxy-managed private endpoints

Thanks Ben / David — Acme security and SRE reviewed the plan. A few clarifying asks before we schedule the 48-hour window: 

1) Per-tenant mapping: our compliance team will accept a signed header only if the header signing key is rotated monthly and we receive key rotation proofs. Otherwise we require NAT-based separation. Please confirm which rotation cadence you can commit to and how you publish rotation proofs.

2) FQDNs and TLS inspection: our perimeter team will only allow 443 to approved FQDNs. For each FQDN you listed we need sample certificate fingerprints (SHA256) so our TLS inspection whitelists can allow passthrough.

3) Ports / ephemeral fallbacks: if we see unknown outbound ports during the test, they will be blocked automatically. Please ensure your runbook includes an explicit list of ephemeral port ranges used by the runtime.

4) Audit delivery: Splunk forwarder is preferred (we can provide a temporary ingestion token); retention 90 days aligns with our policy. Please send tokenized logs only (no PII).

Finally, legal asked that the DocuSign allowlist addendum be signed prior to the test window — I'll route that after we confirm NAT vs header approach.

If Redwood can confirm rotation cadence and provide the certificate fingerprints and the signed manifest, we can target a test window next Tue 06/16.

— Lydia
Head of Security, Acme Health
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Martin <security@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health SRE <sre@acmehealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Outbound binding validation and allowlist acceptance for EdgeProxy-managed private endpoints

Lydia — thanks for the concrete asks, much appreciated. Quick answers and next steps: 

- Key rotation: we can commit to monthly rotation for the signing key used in X-Redwood-Tenant. Rotation proofs (signed statements + epoch metadata) will be published to the Drive folder and we will push an event to your webhook (if you provide one) when rotation occurs.
- Cert fingerprints: David will attach the SHA256 fingerprints for control.redwood.ai and metrics.redwood.ai in the evidence bundle; model-pull endpoints use dynamic certs from Let's Encrypt — we'll provide the chain and the current fingerprint used during the test window.
- Ephemeral ports: our runtime uses system ephemeral ports for backend multiplexing; the only externally visible port is 443. We will add the ephemeral-range note to the runbook, but nothing in our stack requires allowing other outbound ports to the internet.
- Audit delivery: Splunk forwarder is fine — please send the ingestion token to ops@redwood.com; tokenized logs only.
- DocuSign: agreed — please send the addendum link and we'll route legal.

Proposed timeline:
- Fri 6/12: David uploads evidence bundle (redwood-egress-evidence-bundle.zip) and cert fingerprints to Drive + JIRA NETOPS-4271 updated.
- Tue 6/16 08:00-17:00 PDT: 48-hour validation window (we will coordinate exact 48 hours inside that window).

I'll schedule a 20-min ops sync for Monday to walk the runbook and hand over the Splunk token. If that works, can you confirm and share the DocuSign addendum link?

Ben Carter
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood-egress-evidence-bundle.zip (archive), private-endpoint-runbook-v1.md (text)
